quest.title: A Particularly Particular Author
quest.description: Katheryne seems to have a new commission for you.
quest.rewards_formatted: Adventure EXP x450, Primogem x50, Hero's Wit x5, Mora x50000, Mystic Enhancement Ore x4

talks.objective: Talk to Katheryne at the Inazuma Adventurers' Guild

dialogues.speaker: Katheryne
dialogues.text: Your deeds on Seirai Island have been reported to me by Miss Etsuko. You've done very well.

dialogues.speaker: Katheryne
dialogues.text: But back on topic, the Guild has received a commission of even greater difficulty than that which you accomplished on Seirai. I wonder if you'd be interested...

response.speaker: Katheryne
response.text: The person who commissioned this quest is a Miss Sumida. As for the details, it might be best for you to get them straight from her.

response.speaker: Katheryne
response.text: Well then, ad astra abyssosque! I await the completion of your next feat.

response.speaker: Katheryne
response.text: ...You'd consider that sort of commission difficult? Hmm, I suppose I should take that into account next time...

response.speaker: Katheryne
response.text: Regardless, it's not that sort of commission.

choices.text: Even Fatui Harbingers fall before me.

response.speaker: Katheryne
response.text: That is the case, yes.

dialogues.speaker: Sumida
dialogues.text: #Ah, hello there. Might you be the illustrious {NICKNAME}?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: And Paimon's the illustrious Paimon!

response.speaker: Sumida
response.text: Alright then. So, tell me, have you ever "obtained the mightiest sword in the village"?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: The Harbinger of Dawn counts, I guess?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeah, didn't we get that sw{RUBY#[S]Triumphant Harbinger of Dawn that Points Towards Victory}ord from Kaeya that one time?

response.speaker: Sumida
response.text: Hahah, that does sound very strong. Maybe even a bit too deliberately so. Still...

response.speaker: Sumida
response.text: Have you led a life surrounded by beautiful men and ladies?

response.speaker: Sumida
response.text: Well then, did you defeat a giant dragon not long after your story began? Or perhaps, did you get wrapped up in some crisis upon which the survival of a nation hung? Have you ever faced off against "an elite antagonistic force with a numbered ranking scheme"?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Well, I can't say I haven't...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: But hang on, what do you mean by "not long after your story began"?

response.speaker: Sumida
response.text: Or are you, perhaps, in fact a traveler from "another world," just like the main character in "Flowers for Princess Fischl"?

response.speaker: Sumida
response.text: Hmm, I can't feel that sense of "destiny" that a protagonist should have from you.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Y'know, when Katheryne said this was going to be harder, did she mean that communicating was gonna be harder?

response.speaker: Sumida
response.text: Eh!? Wait! Don't go!

response.speaker: Sumida
response.text: Katheryne told me so much about you, so I assumed that you'd be more like a light novel protagonist, you know?

response.speaker: Sumida
response.text: But in truth, I suppose such people are hard to find...

response.speaker: Sumida
response.text: My name's Sumida. As for my pen name... I haven't finished thinking about it yet. I've got plans to take part in this year's "This Novel Is Amazing!" As such, I need a reliable adventurer to help me make a trip to Tsurumi Island.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Tsurumi Island?

response.speaker: Sumida
response.text: #That's right. Now, the name of my novel is currently "The Chronicles of the Sea of Fog." The broad strokes of its plot are as such: a nameless {F#young lady}{M#young man} and {F#her}{M#his} adventures in a nation shrouded in perpetual fog.

response.speaker: Sumida
response.text: Well, the plot details are currently still in the works. But my eventual goal is to write an epic novel that can move hearts and souls, like "Kino's Travels"!

response.speaker: Player
response.text: That's...

response.speaker: Sumida
response.text: Yup, it's that very same "Kino's Travels"!

response.speaker: Sumida
response.text: In which an outlander named Kino who doesn't quite fit in anywhere strides across many strange lands. She meets all sorts of people, and she is drawn into all kinds of wicked plots and all manner of cruel wars. Yet each one of her adventures shall someday coalesce into shining gold...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #Paimon doesn't quite get it, but it does sound like she's talking about you, {NICKNAME}...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: So, about your commission...

response.speaker: Sumida
response.text: Ah, right. Sorry, I got off topic.

response.speaker: Sumida
response.text: Actually, I've been reflecting on that habit of mine quite often. It seeps into my writing as well, to the point where I once wrote over 20 pages before ever getting to the point.

response.speaker: Sumida
response.text: At that time, I wanted to use the legend of the Kitsune Saiguu ushering people into the underground halls of Araumi to save them from a disaster as the basis for a tale about her new incarnation's peaceful life amongst the people of Hanamizaka...

choices.text: So what do you need me to do on Tsurumi Island?

response.speaker: Sumida
response.text: My bad, my bad... So, please go to Tsurumi Island and find a way to bring a Maushiro back to me. This is a traditional instrument of the civilization native to the island, which has been lost for several millennia now.

response.speaker: Sumida
response.text: #As to why I need one, the — fictional, obviously — plot of "The Chronicles of the Sea of Fog (Working Title)" takes place on Tsurumi Island, and when a nameless {F#young lady}{M#young man} sets foot upon it—

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #Let's go, {NICKNAME}.

response.speaker: Sumida
response.text: —They hear a strange sound but it's actually the sound of the traditional Maushiro recording in folktales so please I want to properly describe its sound and that's why I need a real Maushiro!

response.speaker: Player
response.text: You actually stayed on topic.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Nah, she was almost about to go off on some tangent or another. Still, do you really need a real Maushiro just to write a novel, Miss Sumida? Wouldn't a "dududu" or a "phweeet" do just fine if you needed to describe the sound it makes?

response.speaker: Sumida
response.text: Writing is a most serious endeavor. You must treat the things you are describing with the utmost respect.

response.speaker: Sumida
response.text: For example, if you wish to describe Balethunder, you must go to Musoujin Gorge to experience it! That's the only way you can maintain authenticity and credibility!

response.speaker: Player
response.text: That sounds very dangerous.

response.speaker: Sumida
response.text: True, and I almost died back then, too. If I hadn't instructed Kama to get me out of there if he saw that something was going awry...

response.speaker: Sumida
response.text: I was laid up in bed for a few days after that rescue. Everything I could see, everything I threw up... It was all purple.

response.speaker: Sumida
response.text: But now that I think about it, the fact that everything I threw up was purple might've been a result of my only being able to see in purple at the time.

choices.text: Sounds more like you had too much Lavender Melon to eat.

response.speaker: Sumida
response.text: Huh. Now that you mention it, that's true. I should compare and contrast the two experiences next time.

response.speaker: Sumida
response.text: In any case, this letter is for you. Pass it to a man named Kama in Ritou, and he will take you to Tsurumi Island.

response.speaker: Sumida
response.text: Please, this year's "This Novel is Amazing!" grand prize is at stake!

choices.text: And what did you get written?

response.speaker: Sumida
response.text: ...I couldn't get out of bed to write for those few days, so I missed the deadline.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Wait, then wasn't it all for nothing?

response.speaker: Sumida
response.text: How could you say that? This'll come in handy next time if I should ever need to write a convincing scenario like... like "That Time I Was Swallowed Whole by an Electro Slime."

response.speaker: Sumida
response.text: Eh? Wait! I'm sorry! I'm sorry! Don't go!

dialogues.speaker: Kama
dialogues.text: What is it?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Sumida sent us.

dialogues.speaker: Kama
dialogues.text: Another one, huh?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Another?

dialogues.speaker: Kama
dialogues.text: ...It's nothing. Since Lady Sumida has recommended you, I have no complaints. Are you ready to go to Tsurumi Island?

response.speaker: Kama
response.text: Then let us go while the weather remains clement.

response.speaker: Kama
response.text: Come back once you are, then.

dialogues.speaker: Kama
dialogues.text: After two round trips, you should know which way to go now.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Thanks, Kama!

dialogues.speaker: Kama
dialogues.text: No need to thank me. These were Lady Sumida's instructions, after all.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Actually, Paimon's kinda interested to know...

choices.text: Have you ferried lots of people here to Tsurumi Island?

response.speaker: Kama
response.text: I have ferried people and goods to Tsurumi Island, and also to the lands across the ocean.

response.speaker: Kama
response.text: It makes no difference to me. So long as Lady Sumida asks it of me, I will do it.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Sounds like a long story.

response.speaker: Kama
response.text: I've said too much.

response.speaker: Kama
response.text: Well then. Farewell.

response.speaker: Kama
response.text: I owe Lady Sumida.

dialogues.speaker: Kama
dialogues.text: Are you ready to head back?

response.speaker: Kama
response.text: Good. Hop on, then.

dialogues.speaker: Kama
dialogues.text: Are you ready?

response.speaker: Kama
response.text: Then let us go while the weather remains clement.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wow! So this is Tsurumi Island? This...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: ...Looks really sad! What's with this huge fog!?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Kama, do you know that... Uh, what is it again?

response.speaker: Kama
response.text: Yes, Lady Sumida has mentioned it before.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: No! That's not what Paimon means! Paimon's talking about that Maushi-something that Sumida asked us to come look for!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Kama, do you know where we should start looking?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: If he knew, Sumida wouldn't need our help.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Ugh, this is so annoying! Does Paimon have to do everything herself!?

choices.text: I think you're forgetting who does the heavy lifting around here...

response.speaker: Kama
response.text: It's best to enter through that great gate over there, lest you get lost in the fog all too easily.

response.speaker: Kama
response.text: I will wait for you here.

response.speaker: Kama
response.text: Look for me once you secure the Maushiro. I will send you back.

choices.text: All the same, do you have any suggestions?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeah! That's it!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh. Feels like we've gotten our bearings now, huh?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Yup, even though the fog hasn't dissipated yet.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Eh? There's a kid over there...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Do Inazuman kids all run off to deserted islands to play when they've got time on their hands?

choices.text: We should tell him to get to safety.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeah, and let's ask about the thing Miss Sumida asked us to get in the meantime.

choices.text: We can ask if he knows anything about the Maushiro.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Great idea!

talks.objective: Talk to the mysterious young boy

dialogues.text: Yikes!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Uh, I didn't mean to scare you...
You're... an outlander...
And you've got... a little floating girl with you too! That's awesome! I haven't seen any outlanders in soooo long!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Paimon's not a "little girl" or whatever. Paimon's Paimon! And who're you, kiddo?

dialogues.speaker: Ruu
dialogues.text: My name's Ruu!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Uh, either way, the important thing here is...

choices.text: To remind this kid to get to a safe spot.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: No, no, we've got to figure out who the "littler" person is here! How many years old are you, Ruu?

response.speaker: Ruu
response.text: Umm... What does "years old" mean?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: That's the number of years that've gone by since you were born.

response.speaker: Ruu
response.text: The number of years? Let me count...

response.speaker: Ruu
response.text: Several thousand, maybe! Sorry, I can't remember anything more specific.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Uh...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Um...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: How do you count "a year," if I might ask?

response.speaker: Ruu
response.text: Hmm. A year passes whenever I hear the thunder, of course. Just like everyone counts it.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Whaaaa...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: (Hold it just a minute there. Didn't Sumida say that Tsurumi Island's civilization has vanished for several millennia now?)

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: (And his way of counting years is so weird!)

choices.text: (It's probably because they can't see the sun or moon due to the giant fog.)

response.speaker: Ruu
response.text: Still, you've come at exactly the right time! Today's the day of our big ceremony!

response.speaker: Ruu
response.text: Kapatcir will definitely be pleased to have new and rare guests taking part.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Who's that?

response.speaker: Ruu
response.text: My good friend!

response.speaker: Player
response.text: So there'll be a ceremony?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Sounds like a lot of fun!

response.speaker: Ruu
response.text: Exactly! Everyone tells me that I'll be the star of the show this time, too!

response.speaker: Ruu
response.text: But we'll need to do some things before the ceremony can start!

response.speaker: Ruu
response.text: #Either way, {NICKNAME}, Paimon, come with me!

choices.text: (Well, either way, let's hear what the kid has to say.)
To ask about the whereabouts of the Maushiro.

response.speaker: Ruu
response.text: #Ooh, the legendary {NICKNAME}?

dialogues.speaker: Ipe
dialogues.text: Well, that's done.

dialogues.speaker: Makiri
dialogues.text: Nice!

dialogues.speaker: Ruu
dialogues.text: You're back!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: We're back!

dialogues.speaker: Ruu
dialogues.text: The Perch looks really happy. I'm sure Kapatcir will be really happy too!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: That said, who is Kapatcir?

response.speaker: Ruu
response.text: My friend!

response.speaker: Ruu
response.text: Kapatcir loves to hear me sing. I'll be singing for her during the ceremony!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #{NICKNAME} can sing too! Well, {F#her}{M#his} singing turns Glaze Lilies into Whopperflowers, though.

response.speaker: Ruu
response.text: That's amazing!

choices.text: Uh, Paimon, that's not what happened...

response.speaker: Ruu
response.text: Oh, you need a Maushiro? Well, we'll be heading to the ceremonial site soon.

response.speaker: Ruu
response.text: They're going to put all the Maushiro there during the ceremony. I bet Grandpa Mata is going to need help making offerings at the other Perches, too.

response.speaker: Ruu
response.text: Well then. See you both later!

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Not coming with us?

response.speaker: Ruu
response.text: I've got some preparations to make for the ceremony. I'll be meeting Kapatcir there, after all!

response.speaker: Ruu
response.text: Everyone's been looking forward to this ceremony, too! I won't disappoint them!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Well, seeya later then!

choices.text: Mind if I ask about Maushiro...

talks.objective: Go to the destination and talk to Ruu

dialogues.speaker: Ruu
dialogues.text: Let me introduce you to Big Sister Makiri and Big Brother Ipe.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: #Hello there, I'm {NICKNAME}.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey there, Paimon's Paimon!

dialogues.speaker: Makiri
dialogues.text: Hmm~ the Perch seems to be in a good state. This year's ceremony should go well.

dialogues.speaker: Ipe
dialogues.text: Oh come on, less talking, more offering.

dialogues.speaker: Makiri
dialogues.text: After all, the Perch is the keystone to the ceremony. This is the tree upon which the Great Thunderbird once descended.

dialogues.speaker: Makiri
dialogues.text: Grandpa Mata said that the maintenance of the Perch indicates our respect and worship towards the Great Thunderbird. If it is damaged...

dialogues.speaker: Ipe
dialogues.text: I know. That said, this year's ceremony leaves a bad taste in my mouth...

dialogues.speaker: Ipe
dialogues.text: And the fact that I'm the only one doing work over here makes it worse!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: You know what, I think I get this guy.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #Well, you are very reliable, {NICKNAME}.

dialogues.speaker: Makiri
dialogues.text: Eh~ you're just too reliable, Ipe. What's more, this is my first time making offerings to the Perch.

dialogues.speaker: Ipe
dialogues.text: Yeah, yeah, whatever. Anyway, the next step is to touch the Perch. Then, help me look for feathers around this area.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: "Feathers"?

dialogues.speaker: Ipe
dialogues.text: Eh, didn't Grandpa Mata tell you about it? Part of the process is removing all foreign elements from the Perch.

dialogues.speaker: Ipe
dialogues.text: Basically, the power of the Great Thunderbird will accumulate within the Perch, and it will carry off foreign substances that infiltrate Tsurumi Island in the form of "feathers."

dialogues.speaker: Ipe
dialogues.text: Afterward, the fog will purify those feathers. After all, the fog protects our island, and will not let anything pass through the sacred barrier around us.

dialogues.speaker: Ipe
dialogues.text: That's why we need to find the scattered feathers and bring them back to the Perch.

dialogues.speaker: Makiri
dialogues.text: Oh~ I see, I see. I get it now.

dialogues.speaker: Ipe
dialogues.text: ...Did you really?

dialogues.speaker: Makiri
dialogues.text: Probably~

dialogues.speaker: Ruu
dialogues.text: (Big Sister Makiri's just pretending to not get it.)

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: So we just need to find those feathers, right?

response.speaker: Ipe
response.text: So we just need to find some weird looking feathers.

response.speaker: Ipe
response.text: It's made using the Great Thunderbird's power, so if you have keen elemental senses like Ruu does, finding them would be a cinch.

response.speaker: Makiri
response.text: Really? Isn't Ruu lucky~

response.speaker: Ruu
response.text: Hehe.

response.speaker: Ipe
response.text: Don't be silly.

response.speaker: Makiri
response.text: Oh. Sorry.

response.speaker: Ruu
response.text: C'mon, you two. Let's go find those feathers! If you help make offerings to the Perch, I'm sure Kapatcir would be happy.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Uhh... Alright then. Let's just touch that perch first, shall we?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Well, that's all the Perches settled. Guess they can start the ceremony without a hitch now, huh?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Mm-mm, after hearing Ruu talk about it so much, Paimon's getting all excited!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Even if you don't wanna go, we've got to be there if we wanna get that Maushiro.

choices.text: He didn't actually say all that much.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Eh? But he did say a lot about it! You know, like how excited everyone was and how we were welcome...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Eh, whatever! Forget it!

talks.objective: Make an offering to the Perch

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: ...Eh? Where'd he go?

choices.text: I've got a bad feeling about this.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hmm, looks like there's something over there...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Is this the Maushiro?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Nice! Guess Ruu didn't trick us after all!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Well, I suppose that's this commission done.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Still... Paimon feels cheated!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: And what were you cheated out of, exactly?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: They said there'd be a ceremony! And we helped them out with so many things, too!

choices.text: Well, I'm not sure any of this matters other than getting the job done.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: True, but there is one thing that's still very strange...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: There should've been more people here, but it looks like all of them have vanished...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: And all those people felt like they had a few screws loose, anyway...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Whatever. Let's go look for Kama first.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: He should be waiting for us at the entrance.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Anchors aweigh!

choices.text: The happenings on this island are quite concerning.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Paimon thinks there's something odd about this place, too...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hello there!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: We're here to take part in the ceremony.

dialogues.speaker: Mata
dialogues.text: Ah, when will we be ready to hold the ceremony? Preparations for the Perch on Ipe's side should already be complete.

dialogues.speaker: Mata
dialogues.text: He's there with Makiri, so there shouldn't be any issues.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: We've finished making the offerings to the Perch over there!

dialogues.speaker: Mata
dialogues.text: But there are three more Perches. Who knows how the preparations there are going...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: We can go have a look at those.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Where are those three other perches?

dialogues.speaker: Mata
dialogues.text: I hope that... No, the Great Thunderbird will surely be pleased with the ceremony this time...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Eh?

choices.text: What's this Thunderbird you speak of?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Aw, c'mon! Why's he ignoring us?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: We're here to help, too!

choices.text: Could you tell me about the Maushiro...

dialogues.speaker: Sumida
dialogues.text: #Ah, hello there. Might you be the illustrious {NICKNAME}?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: And Paimon's the illustrious Paimon!

response.speaker: Sumida
response.text: Alright then. So, tell me, have you ever "obtained the mightiest sword in the village"?

response.speaker: Sumida
response.text: Have you led a life surrounded by beautiful men and ladies?

response.speaker: Sumida

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Y'know, when Katheryne said this was going to be harder, did she mean that communicating was gonna be harder?

response.speaker: Sumida
response.text: Eh!? Wait! Don't go!

response.speaker: Sumida
response.text: Katheryne told me so much about you, so I assumed that you'd be more like a light novel protagonist, you know?

response.speaker: Sumida
response.text: But in truth, I suppose such people are hard to find...

response.text: My name's Sumida. As for my pen name... I haven't finished thinking about it yet. I've got plans to take part in this year's "This Novel Is Amazing!" As such, I need a reliable adventurer to help me make a trip to Tsurumi Island.

response.text: So, about your commission...

response.text: Actually, I've been reflecting on that habit of mine quite often. It seeps into my writing as well, to the point where I once wrote over 20 pages before ever getting to the point.

response.speaker: Sumida
response.text: At that time, I wanted to use the legend of the Kitsune Saiguu ushering people into the underground halls of Araumi to save them from a disaster as the basis for a tale about her new incarnation's peaceful life amongst the people of Hanamizaka...

choices.text: So what do you need me to do on Tsurumi Island?

response.speaker: Sumida
response.text: My bad, my bad... So, please go to Tsurumi Island and find a way to bring a Maushiro back to me. This is a traditional instrument of the civilization native to the island, which has been lost for several millennia now.

response.speaker: Sumida
response.text: #As to why I need one, the — fictional, obviously — plot of "The Chronicles of the Sea of Fog (Working Title)" takes place on Tsurumi Island, and when a nameless {F#young lady}{M#young man} sets foot upon it—

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #Let's go, {NICKNAME}.

response.speaker: Sumida
response.text: —They hear a strange sound but it's actually the sound of the traditional Maushiro recording in folktales so please I want to properly describe its sound and that's why I need a real Maushiro!

response.speaker: Player
response.text: You actually stayed on topic.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Nah, she was almost about to go off on some tangent or another. Still, do you really need a real Maushiro just to write a novel, Miss Sumida? Wouldn't a "dududu" or a "phweeet" do just fine if you needed to describe the sound it makes?

response.speaker: Sumida
response.text: Writing is a most serious endeavor. You must treat the things you are describing with the utmost respect.

response.speaker: Sumida
response.text: For example, if you wish to describe Balethunder, you must go to Musoujin Gorge to experience it! That's the only way you can maintain authenticity and credibility!

response.speaker: Player
response.text: That sounds very dangerous.

response.speaker: Sumida
response.text: True, and I almost died back then, too. If I hadn't instructed Kama to get me out of there if he saw that something was going awry...

response.speaker: Sumida
response.text: I was laid up in bed for a few days after that rescue. Everything I could see, everything I threw up... It was all purple.

response.speaker: Sumida
response.text: But now that I think about it, the fact that everything I threw up was purple might've been a result of my only being able to see in purple at the time.

choices.text: Sounds more like you had too much Lavender Melon to eat.

response.speaker: Sumida
response.text: Huh. Now that you mention it, that's true. I should compare and contrast the two experiences next time.

response.speaker: Sumida
response.text: In any case, this letter is for you. Pass it to a man named Kama in Ritou, and he will take you to Tsurumi Island.

response.speaker: Sumida
response.text: Please, this year's "This Novel is Amazing!" grand prize is at stake!

choices.text: And what did you get written?

response.speaker: Sumida
response.text: ...I couldn't get out of bed to write for those few days, so I missed the deadline.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Wait, then wasn't it all for nothing?

response.speaker: Sumida
response.text: How could you say that? This'll come in handy next time if I should ever need to write a convincing scenario like... like "That Time I Was Swallowed Whole by an Electro Slime."

response.speaker: Sumida
response.text: Eh? Wait! I'm sorry! I'm sorry! Don't go!

dialogues.speaker: Kama
dialogues.text: What is it?

choices.text: Could we ask you about the fog?

response.speaker: Kama
response.text: Go through the great gate over there. This used to be one of Tsurumi Island's traditions.

response.speaker: Kama
response.text: If not, you'll get lost in the fog very easily.

response.speaker: Kama
response.text: Goodbye.

dialogues.speaker: Ruu
dialogues.text: #Oh, {NICKNAME}!

dialogues.speaker: Ipe
dialogues.text: What's happened?

choices.text: Do you know anything about this fog?

response.speaker: Makiri
response.text: The fog... If it's as Grandpa Mata says, and the fog is so powerful that nothing can invade Tsurumi Island, how do things from the outside get into the Perches?

response.speaker: Ipe
response.text: That's because those foreign substances come from within the ground. The fog can't stop things that come from there, which is why we need to make offerings and purify the Perches.

response.speaker: Makiri
response.text: Huh. And here I thought the fog could do anything.

response.speaker: Ipe
response.text: It's the same for things in the sea. I've fished up some weird stuff before.

choices.text: Hey there, do you know anything about the feathers...

response.speaker: Makiri
response.text: I can't find any feathers!

response.speaker: Ipe
response.text: When you touch the Perch, the feathers will fly to nearby areas. Afterward, you're going to have to rely on your senses. If you've got a good nose for the elements, this should be easy.

response.speaker: Ipe
response.text: It shouldn't be that hard...

response.speaker: Makiri
response.text: But it totally is, though~

talks.objective: Find your way through the mist and make an offering at the Perches

dialogues.speaker: Abe
dialogues.text: Even if it was only just once, I'd love to leave the Sea of Fog and see what lies beyond...

dialogues.speaker: Una
dialogues.text: Are you an idiot? It's utter darkness out there.

dialogues.speaker: Una
dialogues.text: Didn't the priest say that if we leave the fog, our souls will become lost shadows that roam the Realm of Silence beyond?

dialogues.speaker: Una
dialogues.text: If it wasn't for the Great Thunderbird using the fog to protect the island, we'd have been goners long ago.

dialogues.speaker: Abe
dialogues.text: I know, and that's why we hold ceremonies to thank the Great Thunderbird for its protection.

dialogues.speaker: Abe
dialogues.text: ...But aren't you curious about the outside world anyway?

dialogues.speaker: Una
dialogues.text: There were those who tried to leave this place and follow the Great Thunderbird's light to seek new lands. None of them returned alive. You do remember the Kama family's boy, don't you, old man?

dialogues.speaker: Abe
dialogues.text: Oh, how could I forget...

dialogues.speaker: Abe
dialogues.text: Perhaps I simply wish that all went well with him...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: We're back!

dialogues.speaker: Kama
dialogues.text: It's about time you returned.

dialogues.speaker: Kama
dialogues.text: Have you brought the item that Lady Sumida asked for?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: We did.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: It went surprisingly well.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Is something wrong?

dialogues.speaker: Kama
dialogues.text: Nothing. I'll send you back now. Are you ready to depart?

response.speaker: Kama
response.text: Good. Hop on, then.

dialogues.speaker: Onkami
dialogues.text: Where's that Ruu kid gone off to?

dialogues.speaker: Onkami
dialogues.text: Seriously now. It's almost time, and we can't start without him.

talks.objective: Talk to Kama and then return

dialogues.speaker: Mata
dialogues.text: I hope that... No, the Great Thunderbird will surely be pleased with the ceremony this time...

choices.text: Could you tell me about the Thunderbird...
Could you tell me about the Maushiro...

dialogues.speaker: Sumida
dialogues.text: Oh, you're back.

dialogues.speaker: Sumida
dialogues.text: I really hope you've brought the Maushiro this time... Or else...

dialogues.speaker: Sumida
dialogues.text: ...Or else my novel will never get written!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, come on! A commission of this level was a piece of cake for us!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #C'mon, {NICKNAME}, let's show her the Maushiro we found!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Let's finish this commission, get paid, and head over to Kiminami Restaurant for a good meal...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: What? Gone?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: That's impossible! We just got it!

response.speaker: Sumida
response.text: *sigh*

response.speaker: Sumida
response.text: Looks like it happened to you, too... What a headache.

response.speaker: Sumida
response.text: Don't take it too hard.

response.speaker: Sumida
response.text: To be honest, I haven't given you full disclosure either. I did commission other people before sending you.

response.speaker: Sumida
response.text: Adventurers, veteran soldiers, members of Sumeru's Eremites, students of the Iwakura Art, problem-solving specialists from the Yorozuya...

response.speaker: Sumida
response.text: I even hired a very experienced Treasure Hoarder... Went by "Captor" or something. I think he went off to Mondstadt after we parted ways...

response.speaker: Sumida
response.text: Huh, now that I think about it, such a motley crew would've made for a good story. A team of people with diverse backgrounds, characters, and abilities adventuring together...

response.speaker: Sumida
response.text: —Uh, hold on! This isn't the time for such thoughts.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Woohoo, look who's controlled their urge to go off-topic!

response.speaker: Sumida
response.text: Regardless, they, like you, took this job from me, but they all wound up being unable to retrieve the Maushiro that they could've sworn they got.

response.speaker: Sumida
response.text: At first, I thought that they were all just making excuses for their lack of ability. But now that even you, the legendary top-rated adventurer whom the Guild recommended so strongly to me, also encountered this issue...

response.speaker: Sumida
response.text: An unattainable commission, vanishing Maushiro...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: "Would make a good story," right?

response.speaker: Sumida
response.text: ...That is true, but right now, all I want is to finish writing "The Chronicles of the Sea of Fog (Working Title)"!

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Honestly, I'm pretty concerned as well.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Still, Miss Sumida, since Tsurumi's civilization has been lost for so long, there shouldn't be anyone who's heard the sound of the Maushiro, right?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: If you just say that it makes a "phweeet" noise, no one could tell the difference!

response.speaker: Sumida
response.text: The Maushiro, huh...

response.speaker: Sumida
response.text: "When I awoke, a [insert Maushiro sound here] echoed through the bone-ashen fog that surrounded me. I felt as if I were in a dream, so I kept lying there. The sand lay against my cheek, telling me that my dream was set on a beach."

response.speaker: Sumida
response.text: "[Insert aforementioned noise here] grew ever louder, and only then did I recall, like a lightning bolt piercing the fog, that promise I made with a friend. Only then did I recall that this world was not all beaches and sea, but cities and trees also..."

choices.text: I'd give that passage an 8 out of 10.

response.speaker: Sumida
response.text: ...I'm talking about how I won't be able to write this passage if I don't know what a Maushiro sounds like!

response.speaker: Sumida
response.text: As a novelist, this is unacceptable! Unacceptable! Ugh!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Uh, don't worry, Paimon gets you...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh, don't be like that! Paimon's really interested in Tsurumi Island, too...

response.speaker: Sumida
response.text: If you don't mind... I can contact all the other people who took this commission before. Perhaps a discussion might yield some kind of breakthrough...

response.speaker: Sumida
response.text: Don't worry, I won't decrease your pay over this!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #Paimon reckons this is a great idea! What do you think, {NICKNAME}?

response.speaker: Sumida
response.text: Wonderful! You have my gratitude.

response.speaker: Sumida
response.text: Thank you... Thank you so much for your trouble.

response.speaker: Sumida
response.text: I'll contact the people I commissioned before. Give me a while to prepare, and then we'll meet back here.

choices.text: Well, I'm quite interested in investigating Tsurumi Island anyway.
So long as I'm being paid fairly...
I'd probably give this opening a 6.
Eh, I'd give this a 4 out of 10.
What are you even talking about?
I'm not trying to cheat you...

dialogues.speaker: Sumida
dialogues.text: You're back. Do you have the Maushiro?

choices.text: Could I ask about Kama for a moment?

response.speaker: Sumida
response.text: Him? ...Well, it all started when I heard Tang Wen mention Wangshu Inn's Almond Tofu. I thought it would make for a good addition to my novels. For example...

response.speaker: Sumida
response.text: ...Um, I mean. So he's a reliable man who can get you to all sorts of places with eyes. He can even pass through the storms of a sealed nation.

response.speaker: Sumida
response.text: He's got that "keeping his true power a mystery, only to join the protagonist's party in the closing phases of the story" sort of feeling to him, you know? I've worked with him many times.

response.speaker: Sumida
response.text: It is an island to the distant south of Narukami Island, shrouded in a perpetual veil of fog. According to the "Tales of Distant Seas," there were settlements on that island up till several millennia ago, but they were laid waste due to some unknown reason.

response.speaker: Sumida
response.text: Very interesting, no? Uh, I know it's not exactly respectful to say that a civilization's fall is "interesting," but it really does make my writing hand itch! "The Chronicles of the Sea of Fog (Working Title)" is meant to be an adventure title set on Tsurumi Island based on what we already know about its culture...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (Let's beat a discreet retreat...)

response.speaker: Sumida
response.text: Please find the Maushiro... This year's "This Novel is Amazing!" grand prize is at stake!

dialogues.speaker: Kito
dialogues.text: Kina, the old mural that we found previously...

dialogues.speaker: Kina
dialogues.text: Yeah, that's right. That weird round shape, and all those nut-like shapes around it...

dialogues.speaker: Kito
dialogues.text: I asked Grandpa Mata about them. He told me that this was what the ancient world looked like... before it was swallowed up by the darkness.

dialogues.speaker: Kito
dialogues.text: To protect Tsurumi Island, the Great Thunderbird created the great Sea of Fog such that even the darkness would lose its way and become unable to enter the island.

dialogues.speaker: Kina
dialogues.text: ...Yeah, that's cool and all, but what's that got to do with those shapes?

dialogues.speaker: Kina
dialogues.text: That's so weird, right? Not to mention how the priests on the drawings up there don't look like Grandpa Mata or the others at all.

dialogues.speaker: Kito
dialogues.text: Yeah, it's super weird!
